subject: science
intro: I'm Mr. Nakamura, 8th grade physical science. Let's plan an investigation of Newton's second law.

beats.narration: The title hints at the relationship students will discover.
This standard asks students to plan an investigation showing that motion depends on forces and mass.
Planning the investigation is part of the standard, not just doing it.
beats.text: Students will be able to plan and carry out an investigation showing how changes in force and mass affect an object's acceleration.

beats.narration: A prediction commits them to an idea they can test.
beats.text: Show two carts: one empty, one loaded with books. "If I push both with the same force, what happens?" Students predict and explain.

beats.narration: Variables are the backbone of planning an investigation.
beats.text: Introduce F = ma conceptually: more force means more acceleration; more mass means less acceleration. Model identifying independent, dependent, and controlled variables.

beats.narration: Students choose their variable, so there's real ownership of the design.
beats.text: Groups use carts, rubber bands (force), and washers (mass). They design a test that changes one variable, collect data, and graph the results.

beats.narration: Citing their own data ties the conclusion to evidence.
beats.text: Based on your data, what happens to acceleration when mass increases and force stays the same? Cite a number from your data.

outro: Predict, frame, investigate, conclude. Your turn.
